result.note: Tested durable facts on ATF taxation and pricing and ATF's place in refinery output; skipped the airline lobbying and the expected May revision.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to aviation turbine fuel (ATF) in India as of April 2026:
items: Value Added Tax on ATF in Delhi — 29%
Cap on April's domestic ATF base price hike — 25%
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: Delhi charges 25% VAT on ATF; 29% is Tamil Nadu's rate. The excise duty is 11%, and the government capped April's domestic base price hike at 25% even as international fuel prices rose by over 100%.
questions.source: Delhi charges 25% VAT on ATF, Tamil Nadu 29%.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, the Federation of Indian Airlines sought relief on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) costs. Consider the following statements about ATF in India:
items: ATF makes up about 4% of India's refinery output.
Domestic airlines consume most of the ATF produced in India, leaving little for export.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Domestic airlines consume only 30% of the ATF India refines, and the rest is marked for export. ATF now accounts for 55-60% of airline costs, up from 30-40% before April's price hike.
questions.source: Domestic airlines consume only 30% of that, with the rest marked for export.
